newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money edges up to 10.5/11.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money edges up to 10.5/11.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged up to 10.5/11.0 percent from 8.0/9.0 percent on Friday morning.
Dealers said liquidity supply was adequate despite weekly tax payments due on Friday. The central bank supplied only some 80 billion rupiah into the money market this morning.
"Liquidity condition was quite stable in the morning. It should remain at the same later. We didn't see any major purchases earlier," one European bank dealer said.
He explained that the slight increase of overnight money to some early covering because operators did not want to wait until the afternoon.

The central bank offered overnight bilateral papers (SBIs) at five percent, one-week SBIs at 6.5, two-week at 8.25 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 8.62 percent, compared with 11.54 percent on Wednesday.
